To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LSI is not always the best choice in traceability recovery; the size of the repository is the key factor to decide if VSM or LSI are to be preferred; the size and the composition of the vocabulary are not relevant to the decision.

LSI performs worse than VSM in traceability recovery, and this is due to the small number of documents (i.e., artefacts) and the high number of terms (i.e, vocabulary) in software artefact repositories.
LSI is better than VSM when the number of documents is large and the vocabulary is small; and that VSM is better than LSI when the number of document is small and the vocabulary is large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what is the impact of the size and of the vocabulary on the performance of LSI-based trace-recovery?

the following questions: (i) what is the impact of corpus size and vocabulary on the accuracy of LSI-based trace recovery; and (ii) what is the relationship between LSI-based trace retrieval accuracy and the number of terms used in the LSI model.
the role that the size and the composition of an artefact repository plays in traceability recovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of a method to be used for a traceability recovery application depends on the characteristics of the artefact repository to be analysed.
, when dealing with a small repository, VSM performs better than LSI.

LSI is more effective when the size of the artefact repository is large (i.e., more than 500 documents) and when the vocabulary is small (i.e., fewer than 2000 unique terms), while the opposite is true for VSM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the software engineering scenario, LSI performs better when the repository size and the vocabulary are small.
LSI is not suitable for traceability recovery, at least for the moment, because the size of the artefact repository is usually small and the vocabulary is usually very limited.
the use of LSI is more appropriate when dealing with large and rich repositories, while VSM is preferable when dealing with small repositories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LSI is not suitable for traceability recovery in small repositories.
the size of the repository does not affect the accuracy of the LSI-based trace recovery.
, for the considered scenarios, VSM is the most effective method when the repository is large enough to have a good representation of the vocabulary.
